terms.definition: A data structure that stores items (nodes) and the labelled relationships between them (edges). Here the nodes are papers and prerequisite knowledge, and the edges are citations with meaning.
The name of the framework the paper proposes, which builds a knowledge graph of AI papers and uses it to plan learning paths and support idea generation.
A neural network trained on large amounts of text that can read and write natural language. In this paper LLMs extract information, score options and write summaries.
The student-facing application built on GoAI, where students get research trends and learning paths, propose ideas and receive feedback on them.
An account that tells the development of a field as a single chain of events, rather than as a network of interrelated works.
An existing method that a new method is compared against and aims to beat.
Sequences of concepts or skills in which each item must be learned before the next one.
An educational knowledge graph for K-12 schooling that integrates textbooks and educational resources. The paper does not spell out the acronym.
Standard shorthand for school education from kindergarten through 12th grade. The paper does not spell it out.
An online course open to a very large number of learners. The paper does not spell the acronym out.
A neural network that works directly on graph-structured data by passing information between connected nodes.
Language models that are given information from a knowledge graph to improve what they can do, either as text prompts or as processed graph representations.
An online academic paper database with an API that GoAI queries to find papers.
An online repository of research preprints, which GoAI searches through its API.
The top-ranked papers retrieved for a topic, which serve as starting points for building the graph.
A measure of how similar two vectors are based on the angle between them. It is used to compare how close texts are in meaning.
The number of top-ranked papers added to the graph at each extension step.
In the search stage, the maximum number of extension steps in each direction. In path exploration, the beam width, meaning how many top paths are kept.
Big-O notation giving the order of growth of the number of papers retrieved, in terms of K and N, under ideal conditions.
A four-part record. In GoAI it is <paper1, citation position, citation semantics, paper2>, the graph's basic unit.
The meaning or role of a citation, such as extending, contrasting with, or merely mentioning the cited paper.
The location in the citing paper's text where a reference appears, used in the paper as a measure of the citation's importance.
A citation label meaning the paper builds on, extends, applies or is inspired by the cited paper.
A citation label meaning the paper supports the cited work through citation, reuse, supplementation or indirect connection.
A citation label meaning the paper compares itself with the cited paper, proposes alternatives, or restates its content from a different perspective.
A citation label meaning the paper questions, corrects or refutes the cited paper. Despite looking like "question and answer", it does not mean that here.
A citation label for papers that merely mention the cited work or have little direct relevance to it.
A tool that reads scientific PDF files and splits them into structured text such as paragraphs.
A search method that keeps only the best few partial candidates at each step instead of exploring every option. In GoAI an LLM judges which partial paths to keep.
An earlier method (abbreviated ToG in the paper) in which an LLM explores a knowledge graph step by step. GoAI adopts its two-step relation-then-entity exploration.
The step of discarding all but the top candidate relations or papers, here done by prompting the LLM.
An LLM-generated research idea, with motivation, novelty and method, derived from a path. It serves as a stimulus for students and a proxy for how plausible the path is.
A way of getting a language model to reason through intermediate steps before answering. It is also the name of a paper that appears as a node in the paper's example graph.
An evaluation in which several LLM agents each assess the same output and their judgments are combined, here by majority vote.
A decision rule in which the option chosen by most agents is taken as the final result.
The fine-tuned model that reviews the novelty of an idea through three tagged stages: summary, analysis and scoring.
An open instruction-tuned language model with about 8 billion parameters, used as the base for the reviewer.
A fine-tuning method that trains small added matrices instead of all of a model's weights, which makes adaptation cheaper.
An online platform where conference papers and their peer-review comments are posted publicly.
A major machine-learning conference whose papers and reviews are on OpenReview. The paper does not spell it out.
A major machine-learning conference whose papers and reviews were scraped for training data. The paper does not spell it out.
A large language model accessed through an API, used as the backend LLM for GoAI.
A statistic from -1 to 1 measuring how closely two sets of numbers rise and fall together, where 0 means no linear relationship.
A standard questionnaire that rates how easy a system is to use. Higher scores mean better usability.
A standard questionnaire that rates the workload of a task on dimensions such as mental demand, effort and frustration. Lower scores mean lower load.
The amount of mental effort a task demands of a person.
The user-study task of writing a one-page summary of a field's frontier, covering baselines, extensions, contrasts, datasets/tools and prerequisite knowledge.
The user-study task of proposing one or two project ideas on the assigned topic.
